title: Article 219 — Oath or affirmation by Judges of High Courts

content.overview: Article 219 provides that every person appointed to be a Judge of a High Court shall, before he enters upon his office, make and subscribe before the Governor of the State, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule.
content.glance: HC Judge takes oath/affirmation before the Governor (or person appointed by Governor) in the Third Schedule form before entering office.
content.study:
Article 219 oath is taken before the Governor of the State or a person appointed by the Governor, in the form in the Third Schedule.

Examination: before Governor; Third Schedule form; before entering office.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Before entering upon office, every HC Judge makes and subscribes the prescribed oath/affirmation before the Governor of the State or a person appointed by the Governor (Third Schedule form).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Before whom does a High Court Judge take the oath?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 219, every person appointed to be a Judge of a High Court shall, before entering upon his office, make and subscribe before the Governor of the State, or some person appointed in that behalf by him, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule.

examTips: Oath before Governor; Third Schedule form.

keyTakeaways: Art 219: HC Judge oath before Governor.
